subject.title: Clarify or preserve skill source provenance from CLI publish

question: What permanent contract should skill publishing use for CLI-declared GitHub repository and commit fields?
rationale: The current behavior is intentionally safe but ambiguous, and choosing between deprecation, unverified attribution, and a verified publishing flow changes both the product surface and provenance trust boundary.

options.title: Separate unverified attribution
options.body: Retain and expose the fields only as clearly unverified publisher attribution while reserving verification and trust decisions for server-resolved provenance.

options.title: Deprecate skill source flags
options.body: Stop accepting the fields for skill publishing and document GitHub import or another trusted workflow as the only provenance path.

options.title: Build verified CLI provenance
options.body: Add repository authorization and uploaded-file-to-commit verification before storing CLI publishes as trusted provenance.

recommendation.title: Separate unverified attribution
recommendation.body: Retain and expose the fields only as clearly unverified publisher attribution while reserving verification and trust decisions for server-resolved provenance.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged GitHub-backed source work defines the nearest existing trusted path and the implementation boundaries this decision would extend or preserve.
